summary: Kunzang Namgyal was a scholar who studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Kunzang Pelden studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Khenpo Shenga. He later taught Shechen Gyaltsab, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, and Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen.

A scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, Kurt A. Behrendt earned his PhD from UCLA (~1991–1997). At the Metropolitan Museum of Art, he served as Assistant Curator (~2006–2014) and Associate Curator of South Asian Art (~2014).
Working in Indology and related fields, Kurt Andrew Johnson earned his PhD from the University of York by 2010, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Jane Moody.

Kurt Huber studied at Eberhard-Ludwigs-Gymnasium and the University of Munich, completing his PhD (~1913–1917) and Habilitation (~1917–1920). In philosophy, he taught Hans Hartog and served as außerordentlicher Professor (1926) and Professor (1938) at the University of Munich.

Kurt Tropper works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his doctoral degree at the University of Vienna under Ernst Steinkellner, Michael Torsten Much, and Tashi Geisler, later holding posts at the University of Vienna and the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

Kurtis R. Schaeffer studied at Lewis & Clark, Evergreen State, UW, and Harvard (PhD ~1995–2000). Active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he held posts at the University of Alabama (2000, 2004) and the University of Virginia (from 2005).
Kurunegoda Piyatissa was a Buddhist studies figure who served as the head of the New York Buddhist Vihara, with his affiliation attested in 1998 and 2009.

Kwangsoo Park, a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies, completed an MA at the University of Iowa and a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. He held a professorship at Wonkwang University, attested in 2020.

Kyo Kano studied at Keio University, Kyoto University, and the University of Vienna. A scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies, he served as an assistant at Kyoto University (attested 1989) and associate professor at Kobe Women's University (attested 2000).

Kyojun Shimizutani studied at Tendai Sect University and Taisho University. In Buddhist studies, he served as professor at Tendai Sect University (1919) and Taisho University (1926–1945), later serving as abbot of Senso-ji (~1952–1979).

Kyoko Fujii studied at the University of Tokyo. Specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology, she held professorships at Hamamatsu University, Hokkaido University, and the ICPBS, and served as Director of the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (~2018).
Working in Buddhist studies and Sinology, Kyoko Tokuno held posts at the University of Oregon and served as a professor at the University of Washington (attested in 2017).

Kyokuga Saeki was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under numerous traditional teachers, including Reiga, Ryoki Noyama, and Gen'yu. He served as the 143rd elder of Sennyu-ji (~1886–1891) and taught Shundo Sugihara, Eto Senabe, and Eto Sebe.

Kyosho Hayashima was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held teaching posts at Yokohama City University (1962), Toyo University (1962), and the University of Tokyo (attested 1980), and his students included Shinjo Kawasaki and Fumihiko Sueki.
Kyosho Tanaka studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1966 to 1976. In Buddhist studies, he served as an associate professor at Musashino University from ~1976 to 2017.
Kyoshun Todo worked in Buddhist studies. He held academic posts at Bukkyo University, serving as an assistant professor (attested 1962) and later as a professor (attested 1988–1992).

Kyozan Joshu Sasaki studied at Zuiryo-ji and Myoshin-ji under Joten Soko Miura. He was abbot of Yotoku-in (1947–1953) and Shojuan (1953), and later founded Mount Baldy Zen Center, serving as its abbot (~1971–2012).
Kōdō Yamada was a scholar in Buddhist studies who taught at Komazawa University and Keio University.
Kōdō Yotsuya pursued Buddhist studies and Tibetology, earning a master's degree from Komazawa University and a PhD from the University of Hamburg.
